title: Power Pages: create a single-page application (SPA) site from Power Pages studio
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and the Microsoft documentation checked. It distinguishes the planned studio entry point from the documented CLI workflow, and accurately reports the controls, licensing conditions and remaining documentation gaps.

claims.quote: Power Pages: Create Power Pages SPA site from the Power Pages studio

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to let makers create an SPA site directly from Power Pages studio.
claims.quote: Quickly get started with modern single-page application (SPA) development by creating a site directly from Power Pages Studio.

claims.quote: Continue building and customizing your experience using your preferred development tools and frameworks.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Governance guidance; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The studio option's default state and rollout behavior are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages studio create single page application SPA site default enable disable setting prerequisites; studio SPA create prerequisites availability default. Read roadmap, create-code-sites and create-manage; none states the studio option's default or an automatic change to existing sites.

claims.claim: Learn does not yet document the studio SPA creation flow.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages studio create single page application SPA site default enable disable setting prerequisites; studio SPA create prerequisites availability default. Opened create-code-sites and create-manage; results describe CLI deployment and traditional studio templates, not this studio flow.

claims.claim: Requirements specific to the studio flow, including whether the CLI prerequisites carry over, are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages studio SPA create prerequisites availability default. Read create-code-sites prerequisites and create-manage roles; no result describes requirements specific to studio SPA creation.

claims.claim: How the roadmap's studio entry point fits the CLI-only management description is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages studio create single page application SPA site; studio SPA create prerequisites availability default. Read roadmap and create-code-sites, which describes management through source code and CLI; no studio reconciliation was found.

claims.claim: No setting specifically switching the studio SPA option on or off is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages SPA studio enable disable; Power Pages studio create single page application SPA site default enable disable setting prerequisites. Read create-code-sites and control-site-creation; found the general site-creation restriction, not a studio SPA-specific switch.

claims.claim: No admin-center UI path is documented for disablePortalsCreationByNonAdminUsers.
claims.quote: Searched: disablePortalsCreationByNonAdminUsers admin center user interface site creation tenant. Opened control-site-creation; it documents PowerShell only. Other results concerned environment creation or SharePoint rather than this Power Pages tenant setting.

claims.claim: Set-TenantSettings -RequestBody @{ "disablePortalsCreationByNonAdminUsers" = $true } disables site creation by non-administrators.
claims.quote: Set-TenantSettings -RequestBody @{ "disablePortalsCreationByNonAdminUsers" = $true }

claims.claim: Changing disablePortalsCreationByNonAdminUsers to $false allows site creation again.
claims.quote: To enable site creation in a tenant, change the settings value from `$true` to `$false`.

claims.claim: The control's definition of administrator includes the Dynamics 365 administrator Azure role.
claims.quote:
Administrators are the users having one of the following Azure roles:
- Dynamics 365 administrator
- Power Platform administrator

claims.claim: The control's definition of administrator includes the Power Platform administrator Azure role.
claims.quote:
Administrators are the users having one of the following Azure roles:
- Dynamics 365 administrator
- Power Platform administrator

claims.where: controls[0].governs, scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: This tenant-level setting restricts Power Pages site creation by non-administrators.
claims.quote: As a service administrator, if you want to disable site creation in a tenant by non-administrators, you can do it by enabling the `disablePortalsCreationByNonAdminUsers` tenant level setting through PowerShell.

claims.claim: The Power Platform admin center path is Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Privacy + Security > Blocked Attachments.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Manage. ... select Environments. ... Select an environment. ... select Settings. ... Expand Product, and then select Privacy + Security. ... In the Blocked Attachments section, remove `js` from the list of file extensions.

claims.claim: PATCH /organizations(organizationid) is the Dataverse operation for updating the organization record holding the blocked-attachment setting.
claims.quote: | `Update`Event: True | `PATCH` /organizations(*organizationid*)

claims.claim: The update request sets the blockedattachments property.
claims.quote:
### BlockedAttachments
Description: Prevent upload or download of certain attachment types that are considered dangerous.
LogicalName: `blockedattachments`

claims.where: controls[1].scope, note; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocked file extensions are an environment-wide Dataverse control, not a control confined to Power Pages SPA uploads.
claims.quote: You can specify which types of files can't be saved in file columns, attachments and notes. ... It's stored in the Organization.BlockedAttachments column. There's only one row in the organization table.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The documented SPA setup requires JavaScript file uploads to be allowed in the Dataverse environment.
claims.quote: Before you begin, make sure you have: ... Allow JavaScript file uploads in Dataverse environments.

claims.claim: Dataverse describes the blocked attachment extensions setting as preventing upload or download of types considered dangerous.
claims.quote: Block these file extensions | Prevent upload or download of certain attachment types that are considered dangerous.

claims.claim: An SPA site is a Power Pages site that runs entirely in the user's browser using client-side rendering.
claims.quote: An SPA site is a Power Pages site that runs entirely in the user's browser (client-side rendering).

claims.claim: The SPA documentation says these sites are managed only through source code and CLI tools.
claims.quote: Unlike traditional Power Pages sites, you manage SPA sites only through source code and command-line interface (CLI) tools.

claims.claim: pac pages upload-code-site uploads an SPA site.
claims.quote: Use the pac pages upload-code-site command to upload your local source and compiled assets to your Power Pages environment.

claims.claim: An uploaded SPA site initially appears in Power Pages' Inactive sites list.
claims.quote: After you upload a site, it appears in Power Pages in the Inactive sites list.

claims.claim: The uploaded site must be activated to make it available to users.
claims.quote: Activate the site to make it available to users.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model, licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects Power Pages capacity subscriptions, pay-as-you-go meters and qualifying Power Apps or Dynamics 365 use rights.
claims.quote: Power Pages ... licensing is capacity based ... Authenticated user pay-as-you-go meter ... Anonymous user pay-as-you-go meter ... Authenticated users licensed with Power Apps or Dynamics 365 enterprise licenses are granted use rights for Power Pages

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: One Power Pages capacity type is Authenticated users per website/month.
claims.quote: Power Pages ... licensing is capacity based and offers two types of capacities based on user type: Authenticated users per website/month and Anonymous users per website/month.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The other Power Pages capacity type is Anonymous users per website/month.
claims.quote: Power Pages ... licensing is capacity based and offers two types of capacities based on user type: Authenticated users per website/month and Anonymous users per website/month.

claims.claim: Authenticated user capacity is available as a subscription license.
claims.quote: The Authenticated user capacity subscription license can be purchased for the anticipated number of unique, authenticated users.

claims.claim: Anonymous user capacity is available as a subscription license.
claims.quote: The Anonymous user monthly capacity subscription license can be purchased for the anticipated number of unique, anonymous users accessing a website in a month.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Power Pages has an authenticated user pay-as-you-go meter.
claims.quote: The Authenticated user pay-as-you-go meter enables customers to pay-as-you-go based on the actual number of authenticated users who have accessed a website in a month.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Power Pages has an anonymous user pay-as-you-go meter.
claims.quote: The Anonymous user pay-as-you-go meter enables customers to pay-as-you-go based on the actual number of anonymous users who have accessed a website in a month.

claims.claim: The authenticated meter measures unique authenticated users per website per month.
claims.quote: Meter Definition: Power Pages Authenticated user pay-as-you-go meter: A measure of the number of unique authenticated users per website per month.

claims.claim: An administrator must allocate Power Pages user capacity to a Power Platform environment.
claims.quote: This capacity must be allocated to a Microsoft Power Platform environment by an administrator.

claims.claim: Administrators can download Power Pages authenticated reports from the Power Platform admin center capacity page.
claims.quote: Select Capacity. ... In the Add-ons section, select Download reports. ... Select the Power Pages authenticated or Power Pages anonymous report.

claims.claim: Administrators can download Power Pages anonymous reports from the Power Platform admin center capacity page.
claims.quote: Select Capacity. ... In the Add-ons section, select Download reports. ... Select the Power Pages authenticated or Power Pages anonymous report.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Authenticated users with qualifying Power Apps licenses have Power Pages use rights.
claims.quote: Authenticated users licensed with Power Apps or Dynamics 365 enterprise licenses are granted use rights for Power Pages as described below.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Authenticated users with qualifying Dynamics 365 enterprise licenses have Power Pages use rights.
claims.quote: Authenticated users licensed with Power Apps or Dynamics 365 enterprise licenses are granted use rights for Power Pages as described below.

claims.claim: Power Apps per app users can access one Power Pages website in the environment assigned the per app capacity licenses.
claims.quote: Power Apps per app: Users can access one Power Pages website that should be part of the environment to which Power Apps per app capacity licenses are assigned.

claims.claim: Power Apps per user licenses give access to unlimited Power Pages websites.
claims.quote: Power Apps per user licensed users: Users who have been assigned Power Apps per user licenses can use unlimited Power Pages websites.

claims.claim: Dynamics 365 enterprise licenses give unlimited websites that map to the licensed application's context and environment.
claims.quote: Dynamics 365 enterprise licensed users: Unlimited Power Pages websites. These websites must map to the licensed Dynamics 365 application context and map to the same environment as the licensed Dynamics 365 application.

claims.claim: Recognition of Power Apps per-user/premium and Dynamics 365 enterprise licenses requires Entra ID access through the out-of-the-box Azure AD provider.
claims.quote: In order for Power Apps per users/premium and Dynamics 365 enterprise licenses to be recognized: Users should access the Power Pages site using their Entra ID and utilizing the out of the box Azure AD provider.

claims.claim: Those licenses must be assigned in the same tenant as the Power Pages site to be recognized.
claims.quote: Users need a license assigned in the same tenant as the Power Pages site. If the user's license is assigned in a different tenant, it's not recognized.

claims.claim: The SPA page's prerequisites do not name a license.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages SPA single page application licensing pricing meter license. Opened create-code-sites prerequisites: admin privileges, PAC CLI, site version, JavaScript uploads and a local Git repository; no license is named in that list.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No license specific to SPA sites is published, distinct from the documented general Power Pages licensing.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages SPA single page application licensing pricing meter license. Read create-code-sites, Power Platform licensing FAQs Power Pages section and licensing search results; found general Power Pages entitlements, not an SPA-specific license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No meter specific to SPA sites is published, distinct from the documented general Power Pages meters.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages SPA single page application licensing pricing meter license. Read create-code-sites, Power Platform licensing FAQs and Pay-as-you-go meters search excerpts; found authenticated and anonymous website user meters, not an SPA-specific meter.

claims.claim: The documented CLI workflow requires Power Platform CLI version 1.44.x or later.
claims.quote: Power Platform CLI (PAC CLI) version 1.44.x or later installed and authenticated.

claims.claim: The documented CLI workflow requires a Power Pages site on version 9.7.4.x or later.
claims.quote: A Power Pages site on version 9.7.4.x or later.

claims.claim: The site-creation documentation requires a user account with Read-Write Access Mode.
claims.quote: There are some required roles and permissions in Microsoft Power Platform. You need: A user account with Read-Write Access Mode

claims.claim: The site-creation documentation requires the System administrator role.
claims.quote: There are some required roles and permissions in Microsoft Power Platform. You need: ... System administrator role

claims.claim: Where website creation is disabled in the tenant, site creation requires the Dynamics 365 administrator or Power Platform administrator role.
claims.quote: If website creation is disabled in the tenant, users need at least one of the following roles to create a website: Dynamics 365 administrator; Power Platform administrator

claims.claim: The variable cost rating reflects the documented Power Pages authenticated and anonymous pay-as-you-go meters.
